_meta.purpose: Single canonical record of every speculative branch / hypothesis raised by any AI session, user research, or experimental pilot in the Hs / CNT / CNQ project. Each investigation is classified by disposition (CANONICAL / DEFERRED / FALSIFIED / OPEN) and carries gate criteria stating what would (or did) cause it to graduate, fail, or move forward.
_meta.rationale: The framework treats compositional data as a living record where every contribution above the EITT 5% threshold counts as a carrier; below 5% it doesn't make the cut. The same discipline applies to research investigations: every speculative branch is data, and the disposition record is the audit trail. This catalog is the project's research-methodology equivalent of the determinism contract: the path of every idea is traceable.

dispositions.CANONICAL: Met its promotion gate. Lives in the repo. Binding doctrine, code, or schema.
dispositions.DEFERRED: Mathematically coherent or experimentally proposed, but unvalidated. Archived; awaits a pilot or computational verification before promotion.
dispositions.FALSIFIED: Tested (experimentally or analytically) and refuted. Kept on record as part of the audit trail and to prevent re-exploration of the same dead end.
dispositions.OPEN: Raised, in progress, gate criteria stated, awaiting resolution. May be assigned to a person/AI or unassigned.

investigations.title: fit_fixed_point() Period-1 detection symmetric to fit_attractor() — engineering gap
investigations.disposition_note: Engineering gap identified by Grok round 5: Period-1 (fixed-point) detection in CNT is currently asymmetric and indirect, relying on fit_attractor's default fall-through plus Depth Tower energy-tower convergence. A dedicated fit_fixed_point() function symmetric to fit_attractor() would provide quantitative diagnostics (stability_score, residual_variance, convergence_rate, fixed_point_composition) for trajectories that converge rather than oscillate. Important for distinguishing 'truly stable' from 'slowly drifting' trajectories — directly relevant to deceptive drift monitoring.
investigations.summary: Grok identified that fit_attractor() returns period=1 with fitted=False whenever Period-2 evidence is weak — this is a residual category, not an active fixed-point fit. Neither path produces the quantitative diagnostics that would let a user distinguish 'truly stable' from 'slowly drifting'. A symmetric fit_fixed_point() function would compute lag-1 positive autocorrelation (high values = stable), residual variance around mean (low = stable), convergence rate (negative slope of distance-to-mean = approaching fixed point), and return a stability_score + fixed_point_composition + confidence diagnostics. Grok provided a complete Python design that integrates cleanly with the existing attractors module.

investigations.title: Householder formalisation of the metric-dual involution in the CNT Depth Tower
investigations.disposition_note: Paper-worthy mathematical observation: the metric-dual involution M in the Depth Tower (with M² ≈ I) has the same algebraic signature as a Householder reflector (H = I − 2uuᵀ). This provides a bridge between the Depth Tower's recursive structure and classical numerical linear algebra. Grok provided a data-driven Householder reflector construction from ILR trajectory data (leading PC of sliding window → reflection direction → rank-1 update). The construction is sound and could either replace or formalize the current data-derived M operator.
investigations.summary: The Depth Tower's metric-dual operator M satisfies M² ≈ I (involution at machine precision). Grok observed that this is exactly the algebraic signature of a Householder reflector H = I − 2uuᵀ, where u is a unit vector and the reflector is orthogonal, symmetric, and involutive by construction (H² = I exactly, det(H) = −1, eigenvalues +1 with multiplicity D−2 and −1 along u). Grok provided a complete data-driven Householder construction for ILR trajectories: (1) compute leading PC of sliding window → direction v; (2) normalize to u; (3) form H = I − 2uuᵀ implicitly (rank-1 update, never materialize the full matrix); (4) iterate to get Period-2 attractor with amplitude A. This formalization would: (a) give the Depth Tower a rigorous mathematical basis tied to well-understood numerical linear algebra; (b) enable cleaner theoretical proofs about convergence behavior; (c) potentially improve numerical stability through standard Householder implementations.
investigations.gate_criteria: Post-conference theoretical work: paper or technical note formalizing M as a data-driven Householder reflector; demonstration that the current Depth Tower implementation is equivalent to (or a special case of) the Householder-based construction; empirical comparison on EMBER trajectories; potential implementation as alternative path in compute_depth_tower(); citation to classical Householder literature (Householder 1958, Golub & Van Loan).

Strong candidate for a methods paper post-conference.

investigations.title: Yeast Factor diagnostic — 4-phase classifier for latent component power transitions
investigations.disposition_note: Peter's question identified the cross-domain pattern that Grok named 'yeast factor' as a metaphor — Peter then asked whether it could be a real tool addition. investigations.summary: The 'yeast factor' is a real, formalizable diagnostic for detecting components in a pre-activation phase: small raw share but large or growing steering power. Per carrier i, per sliding window τ: yeast_ratio_i(τ) = P_total_i(τ) / max(share_i(τ), ε); yeast_growth_i(τ) = d(yeast_ratio_i)/dτ. The diagnostic produces a 4-phase tag: dormant (low share, low power, flat growth), activating (low share, rising power, high ratio, positive growth — THE YEAST MOMENT), dominant (high share + high power), saturated (power growth ≈ 0), declining (ratio + share falling). promotion_rules.from_OPEN_to_CANONICAL: Investigation must meet its stated gate_criteria. Promotion requires updating disposition, adding canonical_location, and citing the verification record (commit, pilot report, or experiment JSON).
promotion_rules.from_OPEN_to_DEFERRED: Investigation has been considered but pilots are deferred. May reflect resource priority, regulatory dependency, or conflict with current discipline (demonstration-first).
promotion_rules.from_OPEN_to_FALSIFIED: Investigation tested against gate_criteria and refuted. Falsification record must capture: what was tested, what was expected, what was observed, and any reformulation that survives.
promotion_rules.from_DEFERRED_to_CANONICAL: Pilot grounds the speculation. Same gate as OPEN to CANONICAL.
promotion_rules.from_DEFERRED_to_FALSIFIED: Pilot run, refuted. Standard falsification record.
promotion_rules.from_CANONICAL_to_RETIRED: Reserved for future use. Currently no canonical artifact has been retired.

how_to_add_a_new_investigation: 1. Append a new entry to the investigations array with the next sequential id (INV-NNN).
2. Required fields: id, title, raised_by, raised_date, raised_in_push, disposition, summary, gate_criteria.
3. If disposition is CANONICAL, also include promotion_date, canonical_location, and gate_outcome.
4. If disposition is DEFERRED, include deferred_to_location and gate_for_promotion.
5. If disposition is FALSIFIED, include falsification_date, falsification_record, and any reformulation.
6. If disposition is OPEN, include gate_for_promotion and (optionally) promotion_owner and estimated_effort_days.
8. Cross-reference from any new push narrative or AI-refresh document that introduces or moves the investigation.

disposition_definitions.STAGED: Discovery is filed in canon (the doctrine or finding is CANONICAL in content), but file-level ripple through the repo is deferred to a stated promotion window. Used when the doctrine itself prescribes its own staging rule. Distinct from DEFERRED (which means pilots/work are deferred). Distinct from CANONICAL (which means full ripple has occurred). Promotion to CANONICAL happens when the promotion window opens and the ripple is executed.
